about: Each state's permit rules as cited data (#595 PR2; the table #586's fee rules join). Seeded: stateRules.seedStatePermitRules writes these into state_permit_rules and never over a row a person verified (rule 3). Every rule quotes its source. A state is left out of a rule it publishes nothing citable for: Utah, Idaho, Nevada and Arizona publish no statewide prescriptive rooftop-PV path that could be found (as of 2026-11-09), so they carry only the seal rule, and rooftop PV there goes through the standard structural review (permitPath.ts).

rules.citation: Oregon BCD 440-5952 (5/24) Prescriptive Rooftop-Mounted Solar Photovoltaic Installation Checklist, Part III: "If 'No' is selected for any item below, or if the supporting structure is a manufactured dwelling, the project may not be submitted using the prescriptive path."

value: direct attachment to the roof framing or blocking
direct attachment to standing seam metal roofing panels
rules.citation: Oregon BCD 440-5952 (5/24), Part III: "PV modules or racking will be attached to the roof using one of the following methods": Attachment Method 1, "Direct attachment to the roof framing or blocking"; Attachment Method 2, "Direct attachment to standing seam metal roofing panels". Ballasted or non-penetrating racking is attached by neither method.
Oregon BCD 440-5952 (5/24), Part III: "Ground snow load at the site does not exceed 70 pounds per square foot (psf)".
Oregon BCD 440-5952 (5/24), Part III: "Wind exposure for structure is limited to Wind Exposure Category B or C".
Oregon BCD 440-5952 (5/24), Part III: "Total weight of the PV panel system, including modules and racking, will not exceed 4.5 psf".

Oregon BCD 440-5952 (5/24), Part III: "Pre-engineered trusses are spaced less than or equal to 24 inches on center (o.c.); or Rafters are spaced less than or equal to 24 inches o.c. and framing complies with R324.4.1 Exception 1.4 through 1.6".

Oregon BCD 440-5952 (5/24), Part III: rafters qualify only where "framing complies with R324.4.1 Exception 1.4 through 1.6" (Oregon Residential Specialty Code). The span limits of those exceptions are not on file here, so a rafter roof's span is a check with an engineer, never a pass.

ORS 672.020(1): "no person shall practice or offer to practice engineering in this state ... unless the person is registered and has a valid certificate to practice engineering issued under ORS 672.002 to 672.325"; ORS 672.020(2): every final document "shall be stamped with the seal and signed by the registrant."

Utah Code 58-22-602 (Plans ... to be sealed): final plans, specifications and reports of a building or structure erected in Utah "shall bear the seal of a professional engineer or professional structural engineer licensed under this chapter"; 58-22-301 requires the license to practise.

value.board: Idaho Board of Licensure of Professional Engineers and Professional Land Surveyors

rules.citation: Idaho Code 54-1215 (License — Seals): "The seal, signature and date shall be placed on all final specifications, land surveys, reports, plats, drawings, plans, design information and calculations whenever presented to a client or any public or governmental agency."

value.board: Nevada State Board of Professional Engineers and Land Surveyors

rules.citation: NRS 625.383 (Stamp): "Each professional engineer and professional land surveyor shall obtain a stamp of the design authorized by the Board"; NRS 625.381: the Board issues the license to practise professional engineering in Nevada.

value.board: Arizona State Board of Technical Registration

rules.citation: A.R.S. 32-125(B) (Seals for registrants): plans, specifications, plats or reports prepared by a registrant "shall be issued under the registrant's seal if the board requires the registrant to use a seal."
